title: 12. Effects of L-carnitine on heifer serum energy metabolites and body condition score.
content:
Abstract
Assisted reproductive technologies (ART) have the potential to substantially improve reproductive efficiency in beef production systems; however, their success remains variable and may be influenced by preconception nutritional status and metabolic indicators associated with reproductive performance. Supplementation of L-carnitine has been reported to enhance energy metabolism, oocyte and embryo viability, reproductive hormone production, and pregnancy rates in dairy cattle, but little work has been conducted in beef heifers. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of dietary L-carnitine supplementation on circulating energy metabolites and body condition score in growing beef heifers. Eighteen Hereford × Angus beef heifers (n = 9) were randomly assigned to one of two dietary treatments and individually fed using the Calan Broadbent feeding system for 42 days. Isonitrogenous treatments consisted of a basal diet top-dressed with either dried distillers’ grains (CON) or dried distillers’ grains with 100 g of L-carnitine (LC). Body weight was collected every 14 days, and body condition scores (BCS) were taken on day 0 and 42 to assess gain over the study period. Serum samples were collected every 14 days for analysis of non-esterified fatty acids (NEFA) and glucose. There was no treatment × day interaction (P = 0.22) or effect of treatment (P = 0.18) on BCS, while overall heifer BCS increased from day 0 to 42 (P < 0.01). Concentrations of NEFA and glucose remained within normal physiological ranges across all heifers. No treatment × day interactions were observed for NEFA (P = 0.77) or glucose (P = 0.83), and there were no differences by treatment for either metabolite analyzed. However, the relationship with sampling day significantly affected concentrations of both NEFA (P < 0.01) and glucose (P < 0.01). Although L-carnitine supplementation did not alter circulating NEFA or glucose concentrations, additional trials are warranted to evaluate its effects on other energy metabolites and its potential role in enhancing ART outcomes.
